title: BN k222 v1 case: changing nfreq shifts the whole GW window, growing with energy
symptom: First live evolution round (run-20260912T132957Z-53d93fb1e0, everything else frozen): KS bands bit-identical, EXX within 4e-05 eV, but GW states shift monotonically with state index - occupied top ~0.30 eV, mid window 1-9 eV, top state 50.0 eV; only states 5/6 stay put. The raw window is itself unhealthy: QP orderings cross (state 8 below state 7), states reach +212 eV, and a naive whole-window 'gap' is negative.
root_cause: Unknown - do not attribute to the Pade/anacon continuation without evidence (the user explicitly rejects that guess). The shift pattern (small uniform below the gap, monotonically growing above) is consistent with a definitional coupling of the frequency grid to the self-energy evaluation, but the mechanism is open. The window's high states are the fragile part, matching the MnF2 and hBN high-state lessons.
minimal_fix: Do not scan nfreq on this case until the definition is pinned. All recorded diffs belong to the 16->8 direction. Accept near-Fermi states only (window states 3-8); treat the full window as a diagnostic, not an acceptance criterion. A controlled nbands 26->30 probe tests whether adding empty states disturbs the near-gap window at all.
validation: KS bit-identity and EXX invariance prove single-variable control; near-gap window diffs are the acceptance metric. Re-evaluate after pinning whatever definition axis the mechanism investigation identifies.
avoid: Attributing the shift to a specific mechanism (e.g. Pade order) without a controlled test; comparing whole windows containing anomalous high states; treating the old reference window as physical acceptance material.
source: First live evolution round 2026-09-12/13, df pinned stack, ledger /tmp/evolve-bn-run13.json + snapshot state-wise analysis.
